A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoMo research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO and CALVIN experiments, representation analyses, and three-task Franka robot evaluations.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation experiments, five-task Franka evaluations, component ablations, and dual-arm/humanoid action-prediction results.

M1.justification: v2 adds temporal contrastive learning to the existing temporal-difference IDM/FDM. Nearby-future embeddings form positive pairs and temporally reversed embeddings form negatives; an InfoNCE objective supplements reconstruction and perceptual losses. This materially changes representation learning, while the joint diffusion/autoregressive policy framework remains.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained datasets, v2 evaluates RoboTwin dual-arm and EgoVLA humanoid absolute-action prediction. Real-world coverage expands from three to five tasks, adding drawer closing and pouring, replacing combined drawer-opening-and-placement with opening alone, and revising the insertion task.

E2.justification: The LIBERO comparison adds Dynamo and explicitly includes GR00T, corresponding to the retained pre-quantized baseline, while removing DP with five times the labeled data. RGB-Diff disappears from simulation ablations; Tcl-only variants and a naive continuous real-world comparator are added. O2-Fea/Future features and w/o. VQ/Con. are renamed counterparts.

E3.justification: v2 standardizes encoder training on out-of-domain Internet videos, replacing in-domain LIBERO/CALVIN training in the main ablations. The reported CALVIN encoder budget changes from 150,000 to 50,000 steps. The discrete codebook changes from 128 to 8 for LIBERO/real-world experiments, and real-world demonstrations increase from 20 robot plus 20 human trajectories to 25 plus 25 per task.

E4.justification: v2 adds separate Td/Tcl component tests, absolute-action prediction ablations, and cross-environment FDM visualizations diagnosing background leakage and foreground accuracy. Dimension scaling is reexamined through 512 dimensions. The RGB-versus-feature-difference analysis and v1's human-motion cosine-similarity case study are removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports CALVIN means and standard deviations over the last three epochs; v2 reports point estimates without that aggregation description. Deviations also disappear from the LIBERO comparison table. However, the LIBERO ablation table retains uncertainty values and the stated three-run reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced: v1 reports LIBERO averages of 80.8 in-domain and 81.8 with Internet training, versus 80.1 in v2; CALVIN changes from 2.848 to 3.070, with 3.247 at 512 dimensions. These use changed methods/settings, so they are not matched performance gains. New embodiment and real-world results are added. v2 Table 1 also contains an inconsistent discrete S-PCFC average: 0.4810 despite four negative suite values.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 introduces mathematical definitions of three pairwise similarities and their temporal contrastive objective in Equations 1–4. The S-PCFC definition remains equivalent. Neither version provides formal theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list shift from temporal differencing, dimensionality constraints and two new metrics toward complementary Td/Tcl mechanisms and foreground-focused continuous motion. Metrics cease to be a headline contribution, and MSE is attributed to prior evaluation protocols. The central joint-policy-learning and zero-shot-transfer claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 interprets dimensional expansion as introducing noise and motivates limiting motion size; v2 argues that Tcl structures the representation and permits scaling. S-PCFC receives a controlled, motion-centric applicability qualification. Section 6 replaces the explicit gap to fully labeled training and proposed temporal supervision with discussion of modest task-specific policy gains, fine-manipulation benchmarks, and occlusion-related multi-frame/multi-view extensions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a promised project-code address, explicit per-source video counts, the contrastive temporal-offset range, and autoregressive MSE/cross-entropy training details. Appendix A.6 specifies the new absolute-action encodings. Most existing hardware and policy hyperparameters remain documented, while v1's explicit 2,000-video metric-analysis count is omitted. The PDFs do not establish that code has been released.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning by distinguishing CoMo from action-supervised continuous IDMs, including CLAM, and continuous world models such as AdaWorld and DreamDojo. It adds related work including UniVLA, VILLA-X and Dynamo, while removing older discussion of 3D policy approaches. These changes go beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, mechanism explanation, experimental questions, findings and limitations are extensively rewritten. Metrics move from Method Section 3.3 to Experiments Section 4.2.2; Internet training receives a separate subsection. Appendices move before references and gain Sections A.5–A.6. Terminology is revised throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn around Td/Tcl; the metric diagram, cosine-similarity illustration and execution montage are removed. New FDM visualizations, redesigned scaling plots, expanded comparison tables, and updated task/hardware photographs substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The contrastive objective and its component/scaling tests provide stronger support for addressing v1's dimensionality limitation, while new embodiment tests strengthen applicability evidence. These gains are tempered by loss of CALVIN uncertainty reporting and the LIBERO full-data reference, together with v2 Table 1's inconsistent S-PCFC average. The added evidence supports a net improvement, but the reporting regressions limit its extent.
